featured_reviews.review_text:
Stopped by Chai Garam Pocket Cafe in Ghatkopar East (right opposite Jhama Sweets in Rajawadi) for a quick evening bite, and it completely hit the spot! If you're looking for an affordable, cozy place with great hygiene and amazing comfort food, this is a fantastic find.
Here is what we tried:
🍜 Veg Maggi (5/5): Cooked perfectly without being mushy. It’s loaded with fresh veggies like capsicum and onions, and it has just the right amount of flavorful broth. Pair it with their hot kulhad chai!
🍟 Peri-Peri French Fries (5/5): Absolutely loved these. They came out piping hot, super crispy, and dusted with a very generous amount of peri-peri spice. They don’t hold back on the flavor or the heat.
🥤 Oreo Milkshake (4.5/5): Thick, rich, and creamy. It was the perfect sweet, chocolatey balance to put out the fire from the peri-peri fries.
Vibe & Service:
The place is compact but very neat, well-maintained, and has a great, relaxed energy. The staff is polite, and the service is quite fast.
Value for Money: 💰💰💰
Incredibly pocket-friendly! You can easily have a satisfying meal for two here within ₹300–400. Highly recommended for students, friends catching up, or anyone looking for a reliable evening snack spot in Ghatkopar. Will definitely visit again!

We ordered Cheese Peri Peri Fries and two Cold Coffees. The fries were crispy and well-seasoned, and the pricing was reasonable. However, the service was quite slow – it took nearly 45 minutes for our order to arrive, which was a letdown given the small size of the café. Overall, it was an okay experience – the food was decent and the location is convenient, but the long wait time and average beverage quality affected the overall impression. Suitable for a casual stop, but service speed needs attention.

Recently visited ERA77, and it turned out to be a lovely spot for café-style food with a mix of comfort and global flavours.

The Bagel Sandwich was filling and well put together, with great texture and flavours in every bite. Moving to Asian options, the Chilly Garlic Ramen packed a nice punch — spicy, aromatic, and comforting. The Buddha Delight Noodles were equally satisfying, loaded with veggies and clean flavours.

Drinks were a highlight too. The Coffee Mocha was rich and indulgent, while the Classic Cappuccino was smooth and well brewed. To end on a refreshing note, the Berry Blast Boba Tea was fruity, fun, and a perfect pick-me-up.

Overall, ERA77 offers a relaxed café vibe with a thoughtfully curated menu that caters to different tastes — from desi snacks to global bowls and great beverages. Definitely a recommended spot in Ghatkopar for café hopping and casual catch-ups

featured_reviews.name: komal thoria
featured_reviews.review_text:
Finally checked out the new The Rameshwaram Cafe and honestly… it felt like I was transported straight back to Hyderabad. If you’ve ever been to Rameshwaram there, you’ll know exactly what I mean..it's the same buzz, the same chaos, the same aroma of ghee hitting you the second you walk in. And I’m so glad to say, they’ve managed to recreate that exact feeling here in Mumbai.
See Location-wise, it couldn’t get better. It’s literally right at Churchgate, inside the iconic Eros building, barely a minute’s walk from the station...its super convenient whether you’re coming after work or just craving a quick South Indian fix.
The food is CRAZY GOOD! Simple South Indian dishes but elevated with insane amounts of ghee and flavour.
Some absolute must-tries:
Ghee Podi Idli, Benne Masala Dosa,Vada sambhar,Thatte Idli &  Filter Coffee (and even the softy version!) (surprisingly a highlight)
Yes, there’s a wait. Yes, it’s crowded.
Yes, it’s a little chaotic. But that’s exactly what makes it Rameshwaram! :)

featured_reviews.name: shaikh almas
featured_reviews.review_text:
Rameshwaram Cafe is an absolute delight for South Indian food lovers! I tried the dosa, idli, medu vada, and sheera—and every single item was outstanding.
The dosa was perfectly crisp with generous ghee, the idlis were super soft and fluffy, and the medu vada was crunchy on the outside and soft inside, served piping hot. The sheera was rich, flavorful, and tasted freshly made—just the right balance of sweetness and ghee.
And special mention to the tea—hands down one of the best teas I’ve had. Perfectly brewed and incredibly refreshing.
Cleanliness, quality, and consistency really stand out here. Even with the crowd, the service was quick and efficient. Totally worth the hype and a must-visit place for authentic South Indian food. Will definitely come back again! ☕🥞✨

featured_reviews.name: Mili Chikhal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Food:
- garlic chutney flavours nailed
- Benne dosa was small but good — crisp and thick, but honestly places like Krishna Murari also get it right, so it’s not exclusive
- Rassam lacked the flavour bomb a rassam should be it wasn’t sour enough, not peppery, not spicy… just not it
- Sambar: I’ve had better
Masala with the dosa was a joke, exactly 1 spoon and was super bland.
- filter coffee very good
Service:
- Inspite of empty tables in AC, I was made to sit in the gallery just because I was alone
- They do not serve regular water at all even on request, you’re forced to buy PLASTIC bottled water… like why?
- Service staff was humble and well trained but felt like they are trained to ensure good ratings, which is fine, but the food and overall eating experience should genuinely match that
- Dosa took more than 20 mins to arrive
Atmosphere:
-Everything felt very commercial
- It lacks the heart and soul that places like Ramashray, Purnima and even Swati have. I feel food is a business that truly works when it’s served with passion
- For what they charge, it’s not about the money, it’s about how it’s being spent. Maybe spend less on hype and more on actually delivering the experience you are charging for!!!

featured_reviews.name: Dileepkumar Vijaykumar Verma
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited South Indian Cafe and had an amazing experience. If you love authentic South Indian food, this place is a must-visit.
The dosa was perfectly crispy on the outside and soft inside. It was served hot with fresh coconut chutney and tasty sambar. The masala inside the dosa was well-seasoned and full of flavor.
The idli was super soft and fluffy, just like it should be. It melted in the mouth and tasted even better with the sambar. The chutneys were fresh and added great taste to the meal.
The cafe has a clean and comfortable atmosphere. The service was quick, and the staff was polite and friendly. Prices are also reasonable for the quality and quantity they serve.
Overall, South Indian Cafe is one of the best places for dosa, idli, and other South Indian dishes. Highly recommended for breakfast or evening snacks!
⭐ Rating: 4.5/5
